title: Deck Board Calculator
metaDescription: Estimate deck boards, joists, and face screws for a rectangular deck in feet and inches, and check spacing against 2021 IRC Table R507.7 or the 2026 Trex chart.
secondaryKeywords: how many deck boards do i need
how many deck screws per square foot
intent: Estimate deck boards, joists, and fasteners for a rectangular deck, given board size, gap, and joist spacing.
registerRow: Keyword register (estimates): deck board calculator — volume 1, competition ease 4, ad value 3, fit 5, priority 12. Trends ratio vs concrete calculator = 0.008.
intro: Estimate deck boards, joists, and face screws for a rectangular deck. A spacing line compares your joist spacing with 2021 IRC Table R507.7 for wood, or with the 2026 Trex span chart for composite.
chartTitle: Boards for the layout, plus extra boards
heroAlt: Plan view of a rectangular deck: parallel boards with gaps between them, crossing four joist lines.
uniqueAddition: A joist-spacing check against 2021 IRC Table R507.7 for wood, including single span, multiple span, and 45 degree layouts, and against the 2026 Trex span chart for composite, including the 4 inch reduction at 45 degrees and the three-joist rule. A separate table lists boards for four common deck sizes.

inputs.name: length
inputs.label: Deck length
inputs.help: The side you space the joists along, from 4 to 40 feet. Perpendicular boards run this way. The joist count includes one joist at each end of this side.

inputs.name: width
inputs.label: Deck width
inputs.help: The side perpendicular to that board run, from 4 to 40 feet. Each joist is this long. Perpendicular rows are counted across this side. For diagonal boards, length and width are the two outside sides.

inputs.name: material
inputs.label: Material
inputs.help: Composite uses the 2026 Trex span chart. 5/4 wood uses the 1-1/4 inch wood row of 2021 IRC Table R507.7. 2x wood uses the 2 inch wood row. Those names are the nominal sizes in the table. A 5/4 board is often about 1 inch thick, and a 2x board is 1.5 inches thick.

inputs.name: boardWidth
inputs.label: Board width
inputs.help: Face width of one board, from 3 to 8 inches. 5.5 is a common nominal 1x6 face. It was not read from a Trex size chart. Measure the board you are buying.

inputs.name: boardLength
inputs.label: Board length
inputs.help: Stock length you will buy. A stick can cover more than one row when the board run is short enough. A longer run is spliced, and the count tries to reuse an offcut when it is long enough.

inputs.name: sideGap
inputs.label: Side gap
inputs.help: Open space between board edges, from 1/16 in (0.0625) to 1/2 in (0.5). Trex's 2026 guide uses 3/16 in (0.1875) at every temperature and says the gap should stay at or under 1/2 in. Wood gaps are not taken from that guide.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.label: Board direction
inputs.help: Perpendicular boards cross the joists at a right angle. Diagonal boards run at 45 degrees, the maximum angle in 2021 IRC Table R507.7 footnote a. Diagonal changes the board count and the spacing limit.

inputs.name: joistSpacing
inputs.label: Joist spacing
inputs.help: Center-to-center distance between joists. The spacing check compares this number with the limit for the material and layout you picked.

inputs.name: chartSpan
inputs.label: Trex chart span
inputs.help: Used only for composite. 16 in is the 2026 chart span for the common 1x6 boards at 100 psf, and the guide also recommends 16 in for a stiffer surface. 24 in is only for the chart rows that list 24 in. At 45 degrees the guide allows 4 in less than this span. Wood ignores this box.

inputs.name: spanType
inputs.label: Board support
inputs.help: 2021 IRC Table R507.7 footnote c: a board on two joists is a single span, and a board on three or more joists is a multiple span. Trex says composite must span at least three joists. A deck in this size range has at least three joists, so leave this on multiple span unless each board sits on only two joists.

inputs.name: screwsPer
inputs.label: Screws per board per joist
inputs.help: Face screws where a board meets a joist, from 1 to 3. Trex's 2026 guide says two screws per joist. 2021 IRC R507.7 says wood decking gets two 8d threaded nails or two No. 8 screws at each support. Hidden clips are not counted. 1 is below those guides.

inputs.name: waste
inputs.label: Waste
inputs.help: Extra boards for cuts and mistakes, from 0 to 25 percent. 10 percent is a starting estimate. No decking guide supplied that number. For 45 degree boards, raise it if your offcuts are awkward, because that count assumes offcuts can be used.

sources.title: ICC, 2021 International Residential Code, Section R507.7 Decking and Table R507.7 Maximum Joist Spacing for Wood Decking
